messages:
maria: Heads up — after the v3.2.1 rollout started at ~12:05 UTC I'm seeing a sustained uptick in 5xx from hosted inference gateway (~2.7% -> ~9%). Started around the time we flipped the 'seed_route_prefetch' flag in the canary group. :rotating_light:
devon: oncall here, looking. is there a good sample request id / trace id?
maria: trace ids: trace=tx-9a7c, tx-9b2d. quick curl shows 502 consistently for the same prompt. pasted a failing curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -w '%{http_code}\n'```
sam: see same from support logs — customer A reported timeout/errors around 12:07 UTC. Errors show upstream gateway 502 with body: `{\"error\":\"upstream read timeout\"}`.
ops-bot: Deploy started: v3.2.1 @ 2025-11-16T12:04:30Z by sam (deploy-bot). Canary group ~= 5% traffic.
nashley: quick hypothesis: the prefetch flag changes kernel selection and increases memory pressure on canary pods, causing the proxy to hit timeouts. telemetry shows increased LRU evictions on canary hosts.
kate: I can pull host metrics — attaching snapshot of p99 latency and read buffer errors (see link: https://internal.redwood/graphs/abcd). p95 token latency for canary nodes jumped from 45ms -> 220ms.
devon: good catch. can we confirm whether the canary's runtime compiled different kernels? sam, any build tag differences?
sam: yes the canary used kernel-path v2-optimized (opt-kv-v2) as part of the prefetch experiment. Build metadata: kernel=opt-kv-v2, quant=nnq8.
maria: repro steps I ran locally against canary endpoint: 1) set header X-Redwood-Route: canary 2) send a 512-token prompt 3) got 502 after ~3s. Small prompt <64 tokens mostly succeeds. suggests perf issue scales with seq length.
devon: OK — mitigation plan options: a) pause/rollback the flag to remove canary traffic b) scale canary pool + increase request timeout c) pin canary to smaller seq length (not feasible). I'm leaning to immediate rollback to stop customer impact.
support-ash: customers impacted: acct-A (high), acct-C (medium). Support already opened tickets and offered status update. Billing risk: elevated errors may trigger credits.
nashley: agree rollback. how fast can we rollback?
sam: rollback candidate: v3.2.0 stable. Command: `deployctl rollback --service hosted-api --to v3.2.0 --reason "canary prefetch flag regress 5xx"` — will take ~30s to start, but traffic reweight takes up to 3m.
devon: I'll initiate rollback. tagging @kate for observation.
ops-bot: Rollback initiated by devon @ 2025-11-16T12:28:10Z.
kate: monitoring — removing canary traffic now. p99 latency dropping on canary hosts as we shift traffic. evictions decreasing.
maria: after rollback traffic weight at 0% for canary route, errors dropping to baseline ~0.5% within ~2m. customer reports improved.
sam: follow-ups: 1) block kernel-path opt-kv-v2 from canary until perf testing across sequence lengths completed 2) add rollout gating metric for p99 token latency + eviction rate 3) run longer canary with heavy seq-length tests.
devon: agreed. I'll open a follow-up RFC and a postmortem. For immediate next steps: - confirm rollback completed (ops-bot) - notify customers - schedule kernel perf run.
ops-bot: Rollback complete @ 2025-11-16T12:31:45Z. New stable at v3.2.0.
support-ash: sending customer updates now. ETA noted. :white_check_mark:
maria: adding repro logs to the incident ticket and the PR that introduced the flag. Also adding the failing curl output and traces.
kate: opened a short runbook note: "if prefetch flag causes spike in evictions or token p99>150ms during canary, rollback immediately".
devon: filing incident postmortem — will include timeline, root cause (kernel-path + prefetch change -> memory pressure -> proxy timeouts), mitigations. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
sam: TL;DR: bad canary config (seed_route_prefetch + opt-kv-v2) increased memory pressure and token latency for longer sequences, caused gateway 5xx/timeouts. Rolled back to v3.2.0, customers recovering.
maria: closing thread when postmortem links are available.
summary: canary change of prefetch + new kernel caused memory pressure and p99 token latency increase leading to 5xx. rollback to v3.2.0 mitigated. follow-ups: kernel block, rollout gating, perf tests.
